quoted.text: Accelerating scientific progress is one of the most impactful ways AI can benefit society. Models can already help researchers reason through hard problems — but doing this well means testing models on tougher evaluations and in real scientific workflows grounded in experiments.

author: kevinweil
text: I'm excited to see the U.S. move boldly here, and we’re committed to contributing through OpenAI for Science, helping scientists across the country push the frontier of knowledge further and faster. Read more here: https://t.co/Bz0vtJ5sNk

author: kevinweil
text: We’re already seeing early examples of AI accelerating science. With GPT-5, mathematicians, physicists, and biologists are making faster progress on real problems and saving weeks or months.

author: kevinweil

author: kevinweil
text: The White House just launched the Genesis Mission—a national effort to accelerate scientific discovery using AI. It’s a major step toward giving American scientists the data, compute, and tools they need to innovate faster. 🧵 https://t.co/F6cFmtzFcj

author: kevinweil
text:

author: kevinweil
text: 💥 Excited for GPT-5.1, rolling out starting today. It's the best combination of IQ and EQ we've ever shipped. It's smarter and warmer when you just need a quick answer, and calibrates its thinking time to the hardest questions—including scientific research. (GPT-5.1 Pro soon!)
